ops.title: Live TCC durable-identity validation (cc-pool + cookiesync, per Mac)
ops.description:
WHEN: run on each Mac (yBook-Pro + yasyf-home) across TWO consecutive releases to prove the bundle+profile TCC fix — the first upgrade onto v0.59.0 (cc-pool) / v0.16.0 (cookiesync) shows AT MOST one final identity-change prompt per service (the client identity moving from versioned path → bundle identifier); the NEXT upgrade after that must show ZERO prompts. That zero-prompt second upgrade is the definitive proof the user demanded ("fix once and for all"), replacing the skipped VM rehearsal (see note ed5a74dc).

WHAT IT PROVES: a bare Mach-O at a versioned Homebrew path is a path-keyed TCC client (client_type=1) that re-mints every release; the daemon now ships as CCPoolDaemon.app (bundle id com.yasyf.cc-pool.daemon + embedded Developer ID profile authorizing SXKCTF23Q2.ccp) so tccd keys its kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppData grant to the bundle identifier (client_type=0), durable across upgrades. cookiesync gets the same via CookieSync.app (com.github.yasyf.cookiesync) for its AppBundles/Automation grants.

SAFETY: all capture steps are read-only except `brew upgrade` itself. TCC.db reads need Full Disk Access for the terminal (already granted on both Macs). Do NOT tccutil reset unless deliberately re-baselining. R1 open question: if the second upgrade is truly zero-prompt WITHOUT the profile mattering, the Team-ID prefix sufficed; the capture's client_type + csreq columns show which. If ANY prompt survives the second upgrade, capture names the true service/client — the fix then follows that evidence (no more blind keying fixes).

cc-pool v0.59.0 tag: 0ab91806. cookiesync v0.16.0 tag: 4179353. Consent-pending daemon log token to watch: "app-group-container consent" (only fires on an unprofiled build).
